tools.name: list_deals
tools.title: List deals
tools.description: List EVERY deal the signed-in user can see, across ALL pipelines. No implicit pipeline, owner, stage, or status filter is applied — results are only narrowed by the filters you pass explicitly. By default returns a summary column set: id, company, stage (raw pipeline-scoped stage id), stage_label (the human stage name from the deal's assigned pipeline — ALWAYS report this, never the raw id, because stage ids are overloaded across pipelines), pipeline_id, pipeline_name, value, closing_date, created_at, deal_owner, manager, status, updated_at. Pass `fields: "*"` to get EVERY column on each deal (all pipeline-specific fields included — this is how you extract complete deal records in bulk), or a comma-separated column list to choose your own set; use `describe_schema` with table `deals` to see the available column names. Pagination: pass `limit` and `offset`; the response includes `total_count` (matching rows regardless of limit), `returned`, `next_offset`, and `has_more` — keep calling with `next_offset` until `has_more` is false to walk the entire set across all pipelines. The response also includes `pipeline_breakdown` (distinct pipelines present in this page) so you can confirm coverage.

query.description: Substring search across the company / deal name.

stage.description: Stage id (e.g. 'nda-needs-list') or the stage's display label; requires pipeline_id when passing a label.

pipeline_id.description: Optional. Omit to include deals from every pipeline.

created_from.description: ISO date/timestamp lower bound on created_at (inclusive).

created_to.description: ISO date/timestamp upper bound on created_at (exclusive).

closing_from.description: ISO date lower bound on closing_date (inclusive).

closing_to.description: ISO date upper bound on closing_date (exclusive).

fields.description: Columns to return: '*' for every column on the deal, or a comma-separated column list. Defaults to the summary set.

offset.description: Row offset for pagination; use `next_offset` from the previous response.

tools.name: list_pipelines
tools.title: List pipelines
tools.description: List every deal pipeline the signed-in user can see, with each pipeline's id, name, whether it is the default, and its ordered stages (stage id + human label). With deal counts enabled, each pipeline also reports total/active/on-hold/closed counts and a per-stage breakdown using that pipeline's own stage labels, and an extra `unassigned` bucket reports deals whose pipeline_id is null. Global test-deal exclusions (Test-Niki's Store, Example Deal, names starting with 'test ') are applied so counts agree with `get_pipeline_metrics` and the Insights UI.

tools.name: get_deal
tools.title: Get deal
tools.description: Fetch a single deal by id with its full record, linked client contacts, recent status notes, tasks, and attached lenders. Set include_related=true to also return everything attached to the deal: milestones, stage history and stage notes, status notes and report drafts, flag notes, ownership, checklist status, attachments, write-ups, memos (with approvals, comments, views, audit), deal-space notes/documents/conversations/messages, financial data, files, insights and computed metrics, drive and data-room folders, emails and email prompts, client requests, meeting history, links, holds, call transcripts and Claap recordings, calendar items, activity, AI settings and snapshots, research cache, fit profiles, KPI links, SaaS/FinServ models, and task detail (comments, attachments, collaborators, followers, time entries, activity). Always report stage_label, not the raw stage id (ids are overloaded per pipeline).

tools.name: update_deal
tools.title: Update deal
tools.description: Update a deal's stage and/or high-level fields (value, closing_date, deal_owner, manager, narrative, is_flagged, flag_notes, notes = the Status Note box, replaced). Only fields you pass are changed. Returns the updated deal row.

stage.description: Stage id or the stage display label from the deal's pipeline; labels are resolved to the correct id.

closing_date.description: ISO date, or null to clear.

notes.description: Replaces the Status Note text; previous note is archived and the change is logged. Use add_deal_status_note to prepend.

tools.name: add_deal_status_note
tools.title: Add deal status note
tools.description: Add or replace the status note on a deal (the Status Note box on the deal page).

mode.description: prepend (default) keeps history below a blank line; replace overwrites.

source.description: Attribution recorded in the activity log.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks the signed-in user can see, optionally filtered by deal, status, or assignee (assigned_to user id). Returns full row records.

assigned_to.description: User id the task is assigned to.

tools.name: create_task
tools.title: Create task
tools.description: Create a task, optionally tied to a deal, contact, or company. Returns the created row.

assigned_to.description: User id to assign the task to.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.title: Complete task
tools.description: Mark a task as completed.

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts
tools.description: Search CRM contacts by name, email, domain, job title, phone or LinkedIn. Returns a paginated result set with total_count/returned/offset/next_offset/has_more — keep calling with next_offset until has_more is false. By default a summary field set is returned; pass `fields: "*"` for EVERY column on the contact record (all standard and custom fields), or a comma-separated column list. Optional filters narrow by contact type, tag, company, city/state/country, or whether an email exists. Use `get_contact` for one contact's full record plus activities, change history, deals, attachments and suggestions; `describe_schema` lists the available column names.

query.description: Free-text match on name, email, domain, title, phone, LinkedIn. Omit to browse all contacts.

fields.description: "*" for all columns, or a comma-separated column list. Defaults to a summary set.

tag.description: Match a single tag in the contact's tags array.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.title: Get contact detail
tools.description: Return the COMPLETE record for one CRM contact — every column on `contacts` (all custom and standard fields: names, all phone numbers, email(s), job title, geography/city/state/country, LinkedIn, tags, contact type, source, owner, last-contact timestamps, notes and every custom field) — plus its related rows: linked CRM company record, company associations, deals the contact is attached to (with deal name/stage/pipeline), logged activities, full field-level change history, AI field suggestions and their audit trail, attachments, and any funding-source or partner links. Look up by `contact_id`, or by `email` or partial `name` (ambiguous name matches return the candidates to choose from).

include_related.description: Include company, deals, activities, change history, suggestions, attachments and links.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.title: Search companies
tools.description: Search CRM companies by name, domain or website, with optional filters (industry, company_type, status, lifecycle_stage, city, state, country, tag, owner, has_deals). Paginated: returns total_count/returned/offset/next_offset/has_more. Pass `fields: "*"` for every column on the company record, or a comma-separated column list; defaults to a summary set. Omit `query` to browse all companies. Use `get_company` for one company's full record plus contacts, deals, activity history and attachments.

fields.description: "*" for all columns, or a comma-separated column list.

industry.description: Case-insensitive partial match on industry or sub_industry.

tag.description: Match a single tag in the company's tags array.

tools.name: get_company
tools.title: Get company detail
tools.description: Return the COMPLETE record for one CRM company — every column on `crm_companies` (name, domains, industry/sub-industry, type, status, lifecycle stage, employee count/range, revenue/ARR/MRR/contract values, contract and renewal dates, HQ address/city/state/country/postal, regions served, key products, description, socials, phone, tags, owner, source system/external ids, custom fields, notes, timestamps) — plus its related rows: contacts at the company, deals linked to it (with deal name, stage, status, pipeline), full activity history, attachments, team members, contact-to-company match/association history, linked funding sources, tasks, and the parent/child company records. Look up by `company_id`, `domain`, or partial `name` (ambiguous name matches return the candidates to choose from).

include_related.description: Include contacts, deals, activities, attachments, team, funding sources, tasks and match history.

tools.name: create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: Create a CRM contact. Provide at minimum an email or first_name/last_name.

tools.name: create_company
tools.title: Create company
tools.description: Create a CRM company record.

tools.name: search_lenders
tools.title: Search funding sources / lenders
tools.description: Search the master funding-source (lender) directory. By default returns a summary card per lender; pass fields="*" to get EVERY column on master_lenders (criteria, leverage, revenue/EBITDA minimums, industries to avoid, excluded geographies, referral terms, NDA, sync metadata, address, notes) or a comma-separated column list. Filters: name query, deal_size (min_deal <= size <= max_deal), lender_type, tier, appetite_status, active, industry, geography, loan_type. Results are paginated — the response returns total_count, returned, offset, next_offset and has_more; keep calling with next_offset to walk the entire directory. Use `get_lender` for one lender's full record plus contacts, notes, attachments, change history and linked deals.

industry.description: Matches a value in the lender's industries array.

geography.description: Matches a value in the lender's geographies array.

loan_type.description: Matches a value in the lender's loan_types array.

fields.description: "*" for every column, or a comma-separated column list. Defaults to a summary set.

tools.name: get_lender
tools.title: Get funding source / lender detail
tools.description: Return the COMPLETE record for one funding source (lender) from the master directory: every column on master_lenders (criteria, deal size, sweet spot, leverage, revenue/EBITDA minimums, industries and industries to avoid, geographies and exclusions, appetite, referral terms, NDA, sync metadata, address and contact fields, notes), plus its related rows — contacts, notes and note history, attachments, audit/change history, disqualifications, doc flags, fit attributes, pass detections, sync requests, acquisition plans — and every deal this funding source is attached to (deal_lenders rows with deal name, stage, tracking status, quote and status timestamps). Look the lender up by `lender_id` or by exact/partial `name`. Use `search_lenders` to find ids first.

name.description: Name lookup when the id is unknown (case-insensitive, partial).

include_related.description: Include contacts, notes, history, attachments and deal links.

tools.name: update_lender
tools.title: Update funding source / lender
tools.description: Edit every master_lenders column except id, user_id, company_id, created_at and server-maintained updated_at. Does NOT edit deal_lenders or lender_contacts. Only supplied fields change; null clears. Long-text mode replace/append/prepend is atomic with blank-line separation and final length validation. Supports updates[1..25] with independent results, expected_updated_at (conflict returns current lender), dry_run (field diffs, no writes), source and change_reason in each audit row. name renames; name_lookup identifies, rejecting ambiguity. criteria_confidence: imported means unverified imported criteria; null clears. FLEx columns are inert metadata; FLEx stays disconnected.

criteria_reviewed_at.description: When the lending criteria were last reviewed. ISO date (2026-09-14) or timestamp.

criteria_confidence.description: Allowed: imported = imported criteria, not independently verified. null clears.

upfront_checklist.description: Comma-separated list of upfront diligence items, same format as existing rows.

post_term_sheet_checklist.description: Comma-separated list of post-term-sheet items, same format as existing rows.

crm_company_id.description: crm_companies.id to link this funding source to. Must exist and be visible to you.

sync_source.description: Inert historical metadata; does not reconnect FLEx.

tools.name: upsert_lender_contact
tools.title: Add or update a funding source contact
tools.description: Create/update lender_contacts name,title,email,phone,city,state,country,geography,notes,is_primary and CRM contact link. Legacy contact_id targets lender_contacts.id; crm_contact_id writes lender_contacts.contact_id (null unlinks), preserving backward compatibility. CRM link must be in the same company. Primary demotion and per-field audits are atomic. Does not edit master_lenders or CRM contact fields; identity, tenancy and timestamps are server controlled.

lender_id.description: master_lenders.id of the funding source that owns this contact.

contact_id.description: Omit to create a new contact; provide to update an existing one.

crm_contact_id.description: CRM contacts.id; writes lender_contacts.contact_id. null explicitly unlinks. Legacy contact_id above identifies the lender contact row.

tools.name: create_lender
tools.title: Create funding source / lender
tools.description: Create a NEW funding source (lender) in the master directory (`master_lenders`). Use only when the lender does not exist yet — to change an existing one use `update_lender`. Requires `name`; accepts every field `update_lender` accepts. Rejects the request and returns the candidate ids when a lender with the same name (case-insensitive, trimmed) already exists. Applies the same defaults as the app (owner = you, your company, active = true, appetite_status = 'active', sync_source = 'naitive', no tier), writes a 'created' entry per set field to `lender_audit_logs`, and returns the full new record. Contacts go in `upsert_lender_contact` afterwards.

name.description: Name of the new funding source.

criteria_reviewed_at.description: When the lending criteria were last reviewed. ISO date (2026-09-14) or timestamp.

criteria_confidence.description: Allowed: imported = imported criteria, not independently verified. null clears.

upfront_checklist.description: Comma-separated list of upfront diligence items, same format as existing rows.

post_term_sheet_checklist.description: Comma-separated list of post-term-sheet items, same format as existing rows.

crm_company_id.description: crm_companies.id to link this funding source to. Must exist and be visible to you.

sync_source.description: Inert historical metadata; does not reconnect FLEx.

tools.name: delete_lender_contact
tools.title: Delete a funding source contact
tools.description: Permanently remove one contact from a funding source's multi-contact list (`lender_contacts`), e.g. a duplicate or wrong entry. Requires `confirm: true`. Logged to `lender_audit_logs`. Deleting the primary contact leaves the lender with no primary; promote another with `upsert_lender_contact` (is_primary: true) — there is never more than one primary.

confirm.description: Must be true to confirm the permanent deletion.

tools.name: add_lender_attachment
tools.title: Attach a document to a funding source
tools.description: Upload a document (NDA, one-pager, referral agreement, etc.) to a funding source's Attachments, exactly as the app's upload does. Provide the file as `content_base64` OR as a public https `url` to fetch (max 20 MB). Category 'nda' marks the funding source as having an NDA and 'marketing_materials' as having marketing materials in the app. Does not change the legacy `nda` / `referral_agreement` / `lender_one_pager_url` text columns — use `update_lender` for those. Returns the new attachment row.

file_name.description: File name including extension, e.g. 'Acme NDA.pdf'.

content_base64.description: File bytes, base64-encoded (a data: URL prefix is accepted).

url.description: Public https URL to download the file from.

content_type.description: MIME type; inferred from the file extension when omitted.

tools.name: list_lender_attachments
tools.title: List funding source attachments
tools.description: List the documents attached to a funding source (NDAs, one-pagers, referral agreements…) with a signed download URL valid for 1 hour.

tools.name: delete_lender_attachment
tools.title: Delete a funding source attachment
tools.description: Permanently delete one funding source attachment (file and record). Requires `confirm: true`. Only the person who uploaded a file can delete it (same rule as the app).

confirm.description: Must be true to confirm the permanent deletion.

tools.name: add_lender_to_deal
tools.title: Add lender to deal
tools.description: Attach one funding source or a shortlist of up to 25 to a deal. Defaults to on-deck/active; existing links are returned unchanged. Each lender has an independent added/already_on_deal/error result. status sets tracking_status.

tools.name: update_deal_lender
tools.title: Update funding source on deal
tools.description: Edit one funding source's deal-specific row (notes, stage, tracking_status, tags, quote fields, pass_reason) without touching the master lender directory. Target by deal_id + lender_id (master lender id) or deal_lender_id; or pass `updates` (up to 25) for per-item results. Never creates rows.

tools.name: search_deal_notes
tools.title: Search deal notes
tools.description: Search notes attached to a specific deal (deal space notes). Optionally filter by a text query against title/content/tags. Returns id, title, content, folder, tags, is_pinned, user_id, updated_at.

deal_id.description: Single deal. Provide this or deal_ids.

deal_ids.description: Bulk mode: fetch for many deals in one call (RLS scoped). Rows include deal_id.

tools.name: add_deal_note_entry
tools.title: Add deal note entry
tools.description: Prepend or append an entry to a deal's Deal Space note (the notes pop-up), matched by title (default 'Q&A Notes'), creating the note if missing. Never replaces existing content; saves a version and logs deal activity. Use idempotency_key (e.g. a Claap recording ID) to avoid duplicate entries.

title.description: Note title, matched case-insensitively and trimmed.

format.description: text (default): plain text; '- ' lines become bullets, '# ' lines headings, **bold** supported. html: TipTap-compatible HTML stored as-is.

source.description: Attribution recorded in the activity log.

tools.name: get_deal_note
tools.title: Get deal note
tools.description: Read one Deal Space note's full HTML content, by note_id or by deal_id plus title (case-insensitive). Returns candidates if several notes share the title.

tools.name: list_deal_activity
tools.title: List deal activity
tools.description: List recent activity/timeline events — stage changes, field updates, emails, calls, notes, and other logged actions. Pass deal_id to scope to one deal, or omit it to return activity across ALL deals and pipelines the caller can see (RLS scoped). Combines activity_logs (rich events including emails) with deal_activity (structured field changes). Ordered most recent first.

deal_id.description: Optional. Omit to return activity across all deals.

since.description: ISO timestamp lower bound on created_at (inclusive).

until.description: ISO timestamp upper bound on created_at (exclusive).

tools.name: search_deal_documents
tools.title: Search deal documents
tools.description: Search files/documents attached to a specific deal (virtual data room). Optionally filter by name, category, or a text query against name/source_subject/extracted_text. Returns id, name, category, size_bytes, content_type, source, source_subject, created_at.

deal_id.description: Single deal. Provide this or deal_ids.

deal_ids.description: Bulk mode: fetch for many deals in one call (RLS scoped). Rows include deal_id.

tools.name: get_deal_document
tools.title: Get deal document
tools.description: Fetch a single deal document/attachment record by id, including extracted_text when available. Use search_deal_documents first to find the id.

tools.name: search_deal_emails
tools.title: Search deal emails
tools.description: Search email/communication history logged against a deal. Queries activity_logs where activity_type = 'email' for the deal, optionally filtered by a text query against subject, body, from, or to addresses. Returns subject, direction, from/to, sent_at, thread_id, and body snippet.

deal_id.description: Single deal. Provide this or deal_ids.

deal_ids.description: Bulk mode: fetch for many deals in one call (RLS scoped). Rows include deal_id.

tools.name: search_deal_recordings
tools.title: Search deal meeting recordings
tools.description: List Claap meeting recordings and transcripts linked to a deal. Returns recording title, duration, recorder, thumbnail/url, and — when include_transcript is true — the transcript text and summary from claap_transcripts. Optional query filters recording title/summary/transcript.

deal_id.description: Single deal. Provide this or deal_ids.

deal_ids.description: Bulk mode: fetch for many deals in one call (RLS scoped). Rows include deal_id.

tools.name: list_deal_funding_sources
tools.title: List deal funding sources / lenders
tools.description: List funding sources (lenders) attached to deals — the same records shown in a deal's Funding Sources tab. Pass deal_id to scope to one deal, or omit it to return funding sources across ALL deals and ALL pipelines the caller can see (RLS scoped). Optional filters: deal_query (substring of the deal/company name), pipeline_id, tracking_status, stage, lender_name. Each row returns the funding source name, funding_source_type (lender_type from the master directory, e.g. senior debt / sub debt / mezzanine / equity), loan_types, commitment/quote amount, rate and term, stage + tracking bucket (active, on-deck, on-hold, passed, excluded) as status, pass reason, status-change timestamps, and the linked deal_id / deal_name / pipeline_id. Capital-stack position is not tracked as a discrete field; funding_source_type and loan_types are the closest available signal. Results are paginated: the response returns total_count, returned, offset, next_offset and has_more — keep calling with next_offset until has_more is false to cover the entire book.

deal_id.description: Optional. Omit to return funding sources across all deals.

deal_query.description: Substring filter on the deal/company name.

offset.description: Row offset for pagination; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: get_daily_rundown
tools.title: Get daily rundown
tools.description: Read the signed-in user's daily rundown items in display order. Restricted to jturner@5thline.co.

tools.name: add_daily_rundown_item
tools.title: Add daily rundown item
tools.description: Append a new item to the signed-in user's daily rundown. Restricted to jturner@5thline.co. sort_order defaults to the end of the list.

tools.name: update_daily_rundown_item
tools.title: Update daily rundown item
tools.description: Edit an existing rundown item's title, content, sort_order, or source. Restricted to jturner@5thline.co and their own rows.

tools.name: complete_daily_rundown_item
tools.title: Complete or reopen daily rundown item
tools.description: Mark a rundown item as complete or pending. Restricted to jturner@5thline.co and their own rows.

tools.name: reorder_daily_rundown_items
tools.title: Reorder daily rundown items
tools.description: Apply a new display order to rundown items. Accepts an array of {id, sort_order} — only rows owned by the signed-in user (jturner@5thline.co) are updated.

tools.name: list_insights_dashboards
tools.title: List Insights dashboards and widgets
tools.description: List every dashboard available on the Insights page (id, display name, folder, favorite flag) together with the caller's saved widget layouts and any custom (formula-based) metrics defined for the workspace. Use this to discover which dashboards and widgets exist before pulling their data with get_pipeline_metrics, get_revenue_metrics, get_lender_metrics, get_metric_targets, or query_insights_dataset.

dashboard_id.description: Only return layouts for this dashboard id.

tools.name: get_pipeline_metrics
tools.title: Get pipeline metrics (Insights)
tools.description: Compute the deal-pipeline metrics that power the Insights dashboards: total and average deal value, fee totals (total/retainer/milestone), deal counts, and breakdowns by stage, status, deal type, manager, owner, pipeline, and month. Supports a timeframe window on created_at, updated_at, or closing date, plus optional pipeline/manager/status filters. Global test-deal exclusions (Test-Niki's Store, Example Deal, names starting with 'test ') are applied exactly as in the UI.

date_field.description: Which date column the timeframe window applies to.

include_deals.description: Also return the underlying deal rows used in the aggregation.

tools.name: get_funnel_velocity
tools.title: Get funnel velocity / stage durations
tools.description: Return stage-conversion and time-in-stage analytics used by the Insights funnel and velocity widgets. Provide an ordered stage_path (stage ids) to get conversion counts and median/average days between those stages; set consecutive_only to require direct stage-to-stage transitions. Optionally pass deal_id instead to get that single deal's per-stage durations.

stage_path.description: Ordered list of stage ids, e.g. ['nda-needs-list','on-deck','closed-won'].

deal_id.description: When set, returns per-stage durations for this deal instead.

pipeline_id.description: Restrict the funnel to deals in this pipeline (stage ids mean different things per pipeline).

tools.name: get_revenue_metrics
tools.title: Get revenue metrics (QuickBooks / Insights financial widgets)
tools.description: Return the accounting data behind the Insights financial dashboards: invoiced revenue by month, by customer, and by QuickBooks entity (realm), plus outstanding balances, and the P&L snapshots (income, COGS, gross profit, operating expenses, net operating income) for the requested window. Use from/to to bound the period and realm_id to scope to a single entity.

from.description: ISO date lower bound (inclusive) on invoice txn_date / snapshot period.

realm_id.description: QuickBooks entity/realm id to scope to.

include_invoices.description: Also return the underlying invoice rows.

tools.name: get_lender_metrics
tools.title: Get lender / funding-source metrics (Lender Intelligence dashboard)
tools.description: Return the funding-source analytics behind the Lender Intelligence and funnel widgets: counts and quoted amounts by lender stage, tracking bucket (active / on-deck / on-hold / passed / excluded), and by lender name, plus top pass reasons and submission-to-approval conversion. Timeframe bounds apply to created_at or last_status_change_at; test deals are excluded.

tools.name: get_metric_targets
tools.title: Get Insights plan targets and manual metric inputs
tools.description: Return the Master Plan targets (insights_metric_targets: metric key/label, month, target value, notes) and the manually entered metric values (metric_manual_inputs) that the Insights 'Performance to Plan' and 'Variance' widgets compare actuals against. Filter by metric_key and/or a month range (YYYY-MM).

tools.name: list_referral_partners
tools.title: List referral partners
tools.description: Read-only. Lists the contacts currently in the Referral Source pipeline (Sales & BD dashboard) at stages Nurturing, Tier 3, Tier 2 and Tier 1 — the same classification the app shows — with real field values for building email lists: contact_id, first_name, last_name, email, title, company_name, company_id, stage, stage_entered_at, updated_at and owner. Scoped to the signed-in user's company. Sources without an email are skipped and counted in `missing_email`. Every response includes `stage_counts` (per stage, including skipped rows). Pagination: `limit` (default 200) and `offset`; response includes total_count, returned, next_offset and has_more. `stage_entered_at` is derived (no stage history is stored): Nurturing = date added to the pipeline; Tier N = date of the most recent referred deal behind that tier.

stages.description: Stages to include. Defaults to all four: "Nurturing", "Tier 3", "Tier 2", "Tier 1".

tools.name: get_sales_calls_weekly
tools.title: Get weekly sales call counts
tools.description: Returns the Sales Calls metric shown on Insights → Sales Dashboard, bucketed by week (Monday–Sunday, UTC). Debt counts deduped calendar events titled "[Company] <> 5th Line Financing Review"; FinServ counts "5th Line <> [Company] Financial Review". Defaults to the last 12 weeks ending today.

weeks.description: Number of weeks back from end_date.

end_date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to end on; defaults to today.

tools.name: get_deal_hours_fees
tools.title: Get deal hours & fees
tools.description: Hours & Fees for each deal (matches the deal page widget): retainer_fee, milestone_fee, success_fee_percent, closing_fee (total minus retainer and milestone, floored at 0), total_fee, pre/post-signing and total hours, revenue_per_hour, and missing_fee_information. Also returns rollups per pipeline and overall. Filter by deal_id, pipeline_id, stage or company query. Set include_weekly_hours=true for the weekly logged-hours entries (week, phase, hours) behind each deal's totals. Test deals are excluded.

limit.description: Max deals listed (rollups always cover all matches).

tools.name: delete_lender
tools.title: Archive funding source
tools.description: SOFT DELETE: set master_lenders.active=false, preserving contacts, notes, attachments, deal links and audit history. Requires confirm:true and existing lender deletion permission. Refuses deal-linked lenders unless force:true (still preserves links). Never hard deletes or removes stored files. Field diff audited atomically.

tools.name: merge_lenders
tools.title: Merge funding sources
tools.description: Atomic same-company merge: fill empty master fields, reparent contacts, notes, attachments and deal links, transfer audit/history with provenance, then hard-delete the merged master row. Requires confirm:true and existing lender deletion permission. Preserves stored attachment paths. Refuses duplicate deal links, two primary contacts, unique-key conflicts, inaccessible children or remaining references rather than deleting related data. All operations roll back on any failure. Does not use the legacy broad merge RPC or reconnect FLEx.
